Kuvitus: kaupungin katu kesäaamuna. Kadu: Illustration: a city street on a summer morning. In the middle of the street a tram runs along the rails to the right, with motion lines behind it. On the left and the right there are glass tram shelters. Above the tram an overhead wire runs between poles. In the background there are blocks of flats and birches. The picture has no text and no people.
Käsitekartta kolmesta kuvaajasta päällek: Concept map of three graphs one above the other. At the top the position graph, with the straight line of uniform motion and the upward-bending curve of uniformly accelerated motion. In the middle the velocity graph, with a horizontal line and a rising line. At the bottom the acceleration graph, with zero and a constant. On the right, arrows pointing down: the slope of a graph is the value of the next quantity, v = Δx/Δt and a = Δv/Δt. The position graphs are black, the velocity graphs blue and the acceleration graphs orange; uniform motion is a solid line and uniformly accelerated motion a dashed line. On the left, arrows pointing up: the area between a graph and the time axis is the change in the previous quantity, Δx and Δv.
Kaavakuva yhdestä liikkeestä kahtena kuv: Schematic of one motion as two graphs with the same time axis. Below, the velocity graph: the velocity grows uniformly from zero until t1, stays constant until t2 and falls uniformly to zero at t3. The region under the graph is coloured green, and its area is the displacement Δx. Above, the position graph: first a curve bending upwards, then a rising straight line and finally a curve that levels off to horizontal. Over the whole motion the position grows by Δx in total. A blue tangent is drawn at the point P of the curve; its slope k is the velocity v_P, and the same value is marked in the lower graph.
Kuvaaja: junan nopeus v kilometreinä tun: Graph: the train's velocity v in kilometres per hour as a function of time t. Eleven black points at the moments 0–40 s. At the first three points there is a horizontal straight line at the level 90 km/h. A falling straight line is fitted to the other points; it crosses the horizontal line at about 10 s and is extended as a dashed line to the time axis at about 48.5 s. The points (12 s, 85 km/h) and (40 s, 20 km/h) of the line are circled, and the slope, about −2.3 km/h per second, is read from them. The triangle between the falling line and the time axis is coloured green: its area is the braking distance.
Kaavakuva tasaisesti kiihtyvän liikkeen: Schematic of the velocity graph of uniformly accelerated motion, no numerical values. The velocity grows uniformly from the initial velocity v0 at the instant 0 to the velocity v at the instant t, so the graph is a rising straight line. Between the graph and the time axis there is a green trapezium, whose area is the displacement Δx. The parallel sides of the trapezium are v0 and v, and the distance between them is t.
